items.summary_en: New NVIDIA RTX Spark compact desktops from ASUS, Dell and MSI are available today, bringing local AI agents, image and video generation, and model fine-tuning to a dedicated Windows PC. With up to 128GB of unified memory and NVIDIA’s AI software stack, these
items.extracted_title: NVIDIA RTX Spark Compact Desktops Out Now
items.extracted_excerpt: New NVIDIA RTX Spark compact desktops from ASUS, Dell and MSI are available today, bringing local AI agents, image and video generation, and model fine-tuning to a dedicated Windows PC. With up to 128GB of unified memory and NVIDIA’s AI software stack, these
items.extracted_text_for_analysis: New NVIDIA RTX Spark compact desktops from ASUS, Dell and MSI are available today, bringing local AI agents, image and video generation, and model fine-tuning to a dedicated Windows PC. With up to 128GB of unified memory and NVIDIA’s AI software stack, these systems provide room for larger local models alongside RTX-accelerated creative and development tools. A dedicated desktop can keep agents and scheduled tasks running while a laptop travels or handles other work. Alongside the new desktops, an expanding software ecosystem brings more creative and development workflows to RTX Spark laptops and compact desktops. Native Windows on Arm applications from Adobe, the NVIDIA DLSS Ray Reconstruction feature in Blender and local generation workflows in ComfyUI expand what creators and developers can do on RTX Spark — all on one Windows PC. A Windows PC Built for Local AI As workflows expand to include local AI models and agents, more work can continue beyond an active editing session — from generating assets to processing long renders or scheduled tasks. RTX Spark compact desktops give developers, creators and AI enthusiasts a dedicated Windows PC for local models and always-on agents. They bring together image and video generation, model fine-tuning, creative applications and development tools in one compact system. Running supported models locally keeps locally processed code and files on the PC and avoids per-token cloud application programming interface (API) charges for those tasks. RTX Spark desktops are equipped with a 20-core NVIDIA Grace CPU, an NVIDIA Blackwell RTX GPU with 6,144 CUDA cores and up to 128GB of unified memory, delivering up to 1 petaflop of AI performance. Ten-gigabit Ethernet connectivity enables fast transfers of large datasets, model files and creative assets between RTX Spark compact desktops and networked storage. This advanced hardware unlocks incredible capabilities for creators, developers and AI enthusiasts, including: - Running massive 120-billion-parameter large language models locally - Rendering 90GB+ 3D scenes in real time - Smoothly editing 4:2:2 video in real time New compact desktops are available for purchase from ASUS, Dell and MSI, joining the RTX Spark family of laptops available today. Mini PCs from Acer, GIGABYTE and HP are coming soon, along with the Microsoft Surface RTX Spark Dev Box. From Local Agents to AI Creation Native CUDA support and Linux development tools through Windows Subsystem for Linux give developers a foundation for building and running local AI workflows. Developers can set up agents with Hermes Agent or NVIDIA NemoClaw blueprints and fine-tune supported models using Unsloth. RTX Spark can run creative agents that connect familiar applications and local AI tools, helping creators move from an idea to finished work with natural-language instructions. NVIDIA Switchyard, now available in Hermes, automatically routes agent tasks between local and cloud models. Everyday tasks can run on device, while advanced reasoning draws on cloud models, helping manage cloud costs across creative workflows. These capabilities come together in creative workflows that connect Photoshop and ComfyUI through Hermes Agent. Using natural-language instructions, creators can turn sketches into rendered images and animations, or animate an image entirely on device — from isolating a subject and defining its motion to generating the finished video. NVIDIA brought these workflows to life at Adobe MAX, where attendees used natural-language instructions to turn sketches into rendered images and animations for a shared digital Miami landscape. The RTX Video Frame Generation and RTX Video HDR features, already available in ComfyUI, extend the pipeline: a generated clip can be expanded to 60 frames per second and converted to high dynamic range for color grading, all within a single ComfyUI workflow on RTX Spark. Adobe Accelerates the Full Creative Stack for RTX Spark NVIDIA and Adobe are expanding native Windows on Arm support and RTX acceleration across Adobe’s creative applications, helping video editors, photographers, designers and 3D artists work more efficiently on RTX Spark. Adobe Premiere accelerates a range of AI-powered editing features through NVIDIA TensorRT-RTX, including Enhance Speech, Object Mask, Scene Edit Detection and Auto Reframe — so editors spend less time waiting and more time cutting. GPU acceleration also extends to Film Impact transition and effects plug-ins. The update improves support for professional video formats, including Canon RAW, Red RAW, ARRI RAW, ARRICORE, ARRI HDE, H.264 and HEVC in MXF, ProRes RAW and long-GOP video. This lets editors realize more than 50% quicker turnaround on everyday H.264 video deliverables. Adobe Photoshop adds TensorRT-RTX acceleration for the Remove Tool and ArmRTX Spark-native Camera Raw support, helping photographers remove unwanted objects faster and work with RAW images without relying on emulation. At Adobe MAX, Adobe previewed a next-generation image processing engine with extensive GPU acceleration, including interactive Gaussian blur and Light Leaks filters. Adobe Substance 3D Painter 12.2 is now optimized for RTX Spark with native support on Arm for the first time in public beta. Artists in games, visual effects and visualization can run Substance Painter natively on RTX Spark laptops and compact desktops, with no compatibility layer required. Adobe Illustrator and InDesign now offer native Windows on Arm versions optimized for RTX Spark. Adobe Illustrator delivers up to 30% higher performance than its emulated version, helping accelerate illustration, graphic design and page-layout workflows on RTX Spark. Blender 5.3 Adds DLSS Ray Reconstruction to the Viewport Blender 5.3 integrates DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction into the Cycles viewport, helping artists evaluate lighting and materials with near-final-quality ray-traced previews as they work. The practical difference is immediate: instead of navigating a noisy, resolving preview, Ray Reconstruction delivers near-final-quality lighting, reflections and materials in the interactive viewport in real time. DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction support requires Blender 5.3 and the latest NVIDIA Game Ready Driver or NVIDIA Studio Driver. Download the NVIDIA App to get automatic notifications when the latest drivers are available, optimize games and applications from a unified GPU control center, and discover the latest NVIDIA tools and software. Windows Server 2028 Coming to DGX Station for Windows Announced at Microsoft Ignite, Windows Server is evolving for organizations that need to run AI closer to their enterprise applications and data. Microsoft is expanding hardware choice through support for the latest AI silicon, helping customers take advantage of accelerated inference and increasingly capable models in their own environments. NVIDIA DGX Station for Windows platform powered by the GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Desktop
